annotations.title: Explain a light seen in the sky

description: Explain a light someone saw, even days later: compares place and time with the ISS, Tiangong, about 160 bright satellites, planets, the Moon and bright stars, and ranks the compatible candidates. Use it for an imprecise memory; with a measured azimuth and elevation use identify, for a steady point use which_star. Window ±12 minutes, up to 10 days back and 2 days ahead; aircraft, drones, lanterns and meteors are not modelled. A match means compatible with the observation, not proven; the tool never says 'UFO detected'.

az.description: Optional rough direction in degrees from north (90 = east). Improves the ranking.

lang.description: Language of the text fields: fr (default) or en.

lat.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (north positive).

lng.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (east positive). lon and lng are aliases: give one.

lon.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84 (east positive). lon and lng are aliases: give one.

moving.description: Optional: true if it moved across the sky, false if it stayed still. Excludes the other family of objects.

time.description: When it was seen, ISO-8601 with a time zone. Up to 10 days in the past or 2 days ahead.

name: what_did_i_see

outputSchema.description: Returns verdict (compatible | nothing_bright_known | unavailable), best, others, asked.

title: Explain a light seen in the sky
